reason: E1 supports the thermodynamic preference for Al2O3 formation and its role as a dense barrier, but it concerns a multi-element alloy, not a pure Al2O3 coating on Zr-alloy. E2 shows a thin coating (amorphous MEA) reducing oxide scale on a Zr-alloy substrate in high-temperature water, supporting the barrier concept, but the coating is not ALD Al2O3. No cited evidence addresses ALD deposition on Zr-alloy cladding, the specific performance of a sub-micron ALD Al2O3 coating, or its adhesion under the stated conditions.
premises: Al2O3 forms a dense, stable oxide due to its very negative Gibbs free energy
A dense Al2O3 layer acts as an effective oxygen diffusion barrier
ALD can deposit a thin, uniform Al2O3 coating on zirconium-alloy cladding
The Al2O3 coating will significantly reduce oxide scale thickness and weight gain vs. uncoated cladding at ~900 °C
The coating remains adherent and protective under high-temperature steam/air conditions
